newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends down, December at three-week low.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends down, December at three-week low.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures ended sharply lower Thursday, sinking toward the bottom of the day's range on aggressive speculative long liquidation, trading sources said.

Benchmark December futures fell $21 on the day, to $1,362, its lowest settlement since October 4, after ranging from $1,378 to $1,362. Second-position March was down $18, to $1,390, while the remaining months settled $18 to $20 lower.
Origin and outright speculative selling also contributed to losses, traders said, but industry-related buying held December above chart support at $1,360 a tonne.
"There was some scale-down industry buying, but the selling was a little heavier," one trader said.
Technically, December faced stiff support at $1,350, while resistance was noted toward $1,375.
Meanwhile, Ivory Coast launched its 1996/97 cocoa marketing campaign beginning today, and as expected left its key farm-gate price unchanged.
Traders said the Ivorian opening may have weighed on values, with operators holding off sales until the prices were fixed coming back into the market.
Volume on the day was moderate, at an estimated 8,931 lots.
